summary: rbac policy 'not_in' operator fallthrough grants unexpected access when claim missing in private deployment
description: Issue summary: Atlas Retail observed that several service accounts and a subset of human users were granted admin-level routes in their private VPC deployment despite RBAC policies that should exclude them via a 'not_in' expression. Impact: Incorrectly permissive access to admin/config APIs for a small number of identities, risk of configuration changes. Environment: Private deployment (customer-managed control plane), prod-us-east region, customer using SSO via their IdP with claims delivered as JWT to the identity-proxy. Observation window: 2026-03-12 22:30 - 2026-03-13 03:00 UTC. Steps to reproduce: 1) Customer provided a minimal policy that allows action if user.entitlements not_in ["admin", "superuser"] 2) Send request with JWT that omits the 'entitlements' claim altogether 3) Call to /admin/config returns 200 and allowed instead of denied. Expected behavior: Missing claim should be treated as empty set and 'not_in' should evaluate to true for empty set only if semantics intended; policy author expected deny when admin exclusion is required. Observed behavior: Policy evaluator treats missing claim in 'not_in' as a non-match that bypasses exclusion, resulting in grant. Customer impact: Two internal teams escalated (SRE and Platform) and temporarily halted config pushes. No data exfiltration detected.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer defines policy: allow if user.entitlements not_in ["admin", "superuser"]
2) Acquire JWT from IdP that omits entitlements claim (token valid for authN)
3) Call admin API route through identity-proxy and observe 200 OK
4) Inspect policy-evaluator logs and request trace (trace_id: trace-20260313-34b9)
logs: 2026-03-13T00:11:45Z authz-eval INFO allow user=svc-ordering token_kid=abcd1234 trace=trace-20260313-34b9 expr='user.entitlements not_in [\"admin\",\"superuser\"]' claim=ABSENT
2026-03-13T00:11:45Z proxy INFO request forwarded route=/admin/config status=200 trace=trace-20260313-34b9
JWT payload (redacted): {"sub":"svc-ordering@atlas", "email":"svc-ordering@atlas.example", /* entitlements claim not present */ }
comments: Leah Park (Support): Initial report received from Atlas Retail. They included traces and a minimal policy example. Blocking their ability to push config; asked for escalation.
Diego Morales (SRE): Reproduced locally with a mock token. Policy evaluator returned ALLOW when entitlements absent. Created local debug build with extra logging. Tagging eng-authz.

Priya Nair (AuthZ Eng): Looking into boolean ops and value coercion in the policy evaluator. Hypothesis: not_in implementation does a string-contains check and treats absent as empty string which short-circuits differently than spec.

Atlas Retail (Customer): Confirmed workaround of explicitly setting entitlements claim to [] for service accounts mitigates. Requested timeline for patch and whether rollback/mitigation will be supported in their private control plane.
Diego Morales (SRE): Opened INT-4456 to track rollout/patch automation for private deployments. Requested canary rollout to dedicated infra before pushing to private updater.
investigation: Summary: AuthZ engine's expression runtime performs 'not_in' by iterating subject values and checking membership against target list; when claim is absent the evaluator treats subject as a single empty string value leading to membership checks that return false and overall expression evaluating to true. Repro steps run in a dev harness mirrored customer config. Reproduced with token missing 'entitlements'. Additional tests: - token with entitlements: ['readonly'] -> correctly allowed - token with entitlements: ['admin'] -> correctly denied - token with absent entitlements -> incorrectly allowed. Root cause hypothesis: backward-compatible change in the policy-eval library (v2.14.0) introduced value coercion for absent claims. Related PR suspected: https://github.com/redwood-inference/authorization/commit/5f7e2b3. Impact surface: Private deployments that rely on omission semantics for exclusion policies. Risk: Moderate-high for private customers using exclusion-based RBAC.
resolution: Workaround: Advise Atlas Retail to set entitlements claim to empty array for service accounts and short-lived tokens; this required a small IdP mapping change. Temporary policy recommendation provided: add explicit exists(user.entitlements) and deny if not exists. Fix: AuthZ team prepared fix to treat absent claims as empty set in 'not_in' semantics and to avoid coercing absent -> empty string. Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/authorization/pull/869. Deployment plan: canary merge to staging on 2026-03-15, rolling release to hosted and a patch bundle for private control plane customers on 2026-03-18. Follow-ups: document 'missing-claim' semantics in policy language reference; add unit tests for absent-claim cases. Customer communication: emailed timeline and temporary mitigation steps; customer accepted workaround and asked for confirmation post-rollout.
resolution_status: Fix merged to main; private deployment patch scheduled. Customer mitigation accepted; confirm after 2026-03-18 rollout
notes: AuthZ eng to add regression tests for all membership operators: in, not_in, any_of, all_of
Add monitoring alert for unusual increases in admin-route allows per tenant
Prepare KB article for private customers about claim absence semantics and policy patterns
